title: Sunspots, solar flux, K and A
idea: Sunspots and solar flux tell you how high the bands go. K and A tell you how stormy Earth's magnetic field is.

compare.how: Sunspots and solar flux: higher means the higher frequencies work better.
K and A: how disturbed Earth's magnetic field is. Higher is worse.
The workhorse: open by day at any point in the solar cycle.

traps.wrong: A zero sunspot number indicates that radio propagation is not possible on any band
traps.why: Low bands and 20 meters still work. It's the higher bands that close.
Low solar activity closes the high bands: 15, 12 and 10 meters.

traps.wrong: A count of sunspots that is adjusted for solar emissions
traps.why: It's radio noise at a wavelength of 10.7 centimeters, not a count.
20 meters works by day at any point in the cycle.

traps.wrong: The short-term stability of the Sun’s magnetic field
traps.why: K is about Earth's magnetic field, not the Sun's.

traps.wrong: The solar radio flux at Boulder, Colorado
traps.why: A is the long-term stability of Earth's magnetic field.
